item.title: One Human, a Board and a Team of Agents: How I Build Software Now (and Why My Estimate Was Wrong)
item.description: The estimate said one human with four agents would need 76 weeks to build Horae, where three developers need 22. All the work agents could do was finished in 15 days. On both projects agents needed a third to a sixth of the estimated time, and nobody took over in 123 recorded stories. The bottleneck is still the human, but not where the model put it: in the tickets, the decisions, the quota and the first real deployment.
